text:
alex: Heads up — seeing an intermittent p99 spike on the /v1/rerank endpoint in the replay harness after switching the default kernel to the int8-optimized path. Repro steps and quick traces below.

maria: Oof, how big are the batches when it spikes? Any correlation with vector dim or payload size?

alex: Mostly B=8-16 in the harness, payloads ~24-48KB (variable number of documents). Model is the 1536-dim ranker we deployed last month. Baseline (float16 generic kernels): p50 18ms p95 52ms p99 135ms. With int8 fused kernels: p50 16ms p95 55ms p99 250-420ms (very noisy).

alex: Quick profiling snippet (nvprof-ish stack samples):
```
[GPU] 40% time: fused_attn_v2_forward
[GPU] 22% time: generic_gemm
[CPU] 18% time: batcher_coalesce_wait
[CPU] 12% time: kv_cache_lock_wait
```

tj: kv_cache_lock_wait stands out. Are we seeing evictions or cache churn with the replay traffic?

alex: Yes — the replay harness uses many short prefixes which defeats prefix caching and causes a lot of small KV set/get traffic. Cache hit rate drops from ~82% to ~46% in the worst runs.

zoe: Could the int8 kernel be more sensitive to input alignment/sequence-length packing, causing variance when batcher coalesces different lengths? We changed the binning heuristic last week.

samir: Agree. Packing variance + fused kernels = different kernel selection and memory access patterns => tail amplification. I remember we disabled the length-aware packer in the canary.

alex: TL;DR hypothesis: new batcher heuristic plus int8 fused kernel results in less homogeneous batches, more KV contention, and occasional path that triggers a slow fallback in fused_attn_v2 (locks + cross-block sync).

maria: Proposal for steps to isolate (minimal blast radius):
- Run controlled replay with fixed prefix set to keep KV hit rate >95%
- Sweep batch sizes B=[4,8,16,32] and packing modes (strict-pad vs mixed-pack)
- Toggle kernel selection: forced_generic, forced_fused_int8, auto
- Capture flamegraphs + per-request kernel selection logs (enable TRACE_KSEL=1)

alex: Can someone run the above on the 8xA100 test cluster? benchbot, can you kick a job?

benchbot: job 20260318-0811 queued (ranker-kernel-sweep). ETA ~12m. Config: harness=replay, seeds=5, batch_sizes=[4,8,16,32], model_dim=1536, payloads=[24KB,48KB], packer_modes=[strict,mixed], kernels=[auto,forced_generic,forced_fused_int8].

tj: I'll instrument the KV layer to log per-request hit/miss and lock wait times (low-overhead counters). Sharing a patch in a sec.

zoe: Also pls collect per-kernel SM occupancy and L2 dram throughput — that helped last time to spot a bad memory access pattern.

samir: If we confirm it's batching causing the issue, we can adjust the heuristic: prioritize length-homogeneity for rerank endpoints (they're latency sensitive) and fallback to generic kernel for mixed batches.

alex: One more note — observed a small perf regression on small batch float16 synthetic too after last scheduler change (p95 +8%). Might be related to how we schedule micro-batches onto CUDA streams. Add that to the sweep.

maria: Thanks. If bench results show fused_int8 loses on p99 for mixed packs but wins on p50/p95 for strict packs, then recommendation = auto kernel with conservative threshold: if packing_entropy > 0.3 use generic. We'll need a perf test and a small rollout.

ops-bot: Metric alert resolved — rerank.p99 > 300ms (us-west) returned to normal after canary rollback.

alex: benchbot posted results: https://internal/bench/20260318-0811 (summary below). Key takeaways:
- forced_fused_int8 + mixed-pack: p99 = 410ms, KV hit=47%
- forced_fused_int8 + strict-pack: p99 = 120ms, KV hit=90%
- forced_generic + mixed-pack: p99 = 140ms, KV hit=49%
- auto: picks fused for ~65% of batches; p99 = 190ms

alex: Conclusion from run: the fused int8 kernel is fine when batches are homogeneous. Mixed packing + fused triggers pathological slow path (probably due to padding-handling kernel path + increased locks). Generic kernel is more stable for mixed batches.

maria: Action items:
- Implement packing_entropy metric, expose to runtime telemetry (eng-runtime team)
- Change default auto policy: prefer generic when entropy >= 0.25 for rerank route
- Add new e2e test in harnesses to include mixed-pack replay and assert p99 < 200ms
- Roll a canary with these changes to dedicated region

tj: I'll push a small change to the batcher + add smoke test. One open Q: does switching to generic for mixed batches increase cost too much? Need cost sim of token throughput.

samir: I can run a cost/latency tradeoff sim (cheap) — will post numbers here.

zoe: Nice detective work. Please include a short postmortem blurb once the canary is stable so Product/SRE can update runbooks.

alex: Thanks all. Leaving the thread open for bench results and the canary.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started for rerank kernel-policy update to us-west-dedicated. Canary id=cr-20260318-2.

benchbot: final note: artifact bundles (traces + flamegraphs) uploaded to https://internal/artifacts/cr-20260318-2/ (30MB).
